mechanism_narrative: The t-0 week is a single-week confinement impulse, not a regime shift: RESIDENTIAL jumps 6.2 points to 12.1 while RETAIL_REC falls 15.3 points in the same week. Because home-stay impulses of this size decay within about two weeks, time-at-home mean-reverts and RETAIL_REC returns toward its -20 three-week plateau, which sits above the -24.2 trailing 28-day mean that the shock week drags down.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 5.9 to 12.1 in the final week while RETAIL_REC fell from -20.4 to -35.7
regime_hint: steady state with a one-week home-stay impulse
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 10 in the next two weekly prints while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below -24.2.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT prints -59.7, the lowest of the four weeks and 12.7 points below the prior week. Transit stations carry the trip-chaining that feeds multi-stop retail districts, and retail visits lag transit troughs rather than leading them, so RETAIL_REC stays below the -24.2 trailing 28-day mean across the whole four-week window instead of rebounding.
failure_condition: The next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds -24.2 while TRANSIT remains below -55 for two or more of those weekly prints.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week transit drop greater than 10 points is the signature of a newly imposed stay-at-home order rather than voluntary caution. When TRANSIT crosses from -47.0 to -59.7 and WORKPLACES simultaneously relapses from -17.7 to -29.9, the retail decline is policy-forced and persists at least through the following weekly print, keeping RETAIL_REC below the -24.2 trailing mean over the next 28 days.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week (from -47.0 to -59.7) with WORKPLACES falling more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 12.7 points and WORKPLACES fell 12.2 points in the final week
failure_condition: The next weekly RETAIL_REC print is above -20 and the first two weekly prints after t-0 are both above -24.2 despite TRANSIT staying below -55.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime the WORKPLACES series is the leading edge of re-closure: it rose to -17.7 and then relapsed to -29.9, below the previous trough of -26.4. Office vacancy removes weekday lunchtime and after-work retail demand, so re-closure propagates into RETAIL_REC with roughly a two-week lag and keeps the next-28-day mean below the trailing -24.2 value.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls back below -25 after a weekly print above -20
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES printed -17.7 at t-1w then -29.9 at t-0w, a lower low than the -26.4 at t-3w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES holds below -25 for the next two weekly prints while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is above -24.2.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signal of PARKS at -27.4 and RESIDENTIAL at 12.1 identifies substitution of out-of-home leisure by home time. The interaction matters because PARKS alone can fall from weather while RESIDENTIAL alone can rise from remote work; only their coincidence implies that leisure-bundled retail trips are being cancelled, pushing RETAIL_REC further down over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -25 and RESIDENTIAL above 10 in the same weekly print
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w PARKS equals -27.4 and RESIDENTIAL equals 12.1
regime_hint: tightening restrictions with cold-weather outdoor suppression
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS is below -25 and RESIDENTIAL above 10, the two-week-ahead RETAIL_REC print is above the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM at -10.1 is the least-depressed non-residential category, showing essential errands still occur, while TRANSIT below -55 shows long-distance trip chains have collapsed. The interaction means remaining out-of-home trips are short and local, and because grocery anchors sit inside retail strips, the trip residue lifts adjacent retail visits, producing a one-week RETAIL_REC print above -35.7.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -55 and GROCERY_PHARM at or above -12 in the same weekly print
evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w GROCERY_PHARM equals -10.1 and TRANSIT equals -59.7
failure_condition: The next weekly RETAIL_REC print is at or below -35.7 while TRANSIT remains below -55 and GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above -12.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS falling from -5.3 at t-3w to -27.4 at t-0w is a seasonal cold-weather contraction of outdoor activity, not a demand collapse. Once PARKS crosses below -25, leisure spending that would have occurred outdoors is redirected into indoor commercial venues such as restaurants, gyms and shops, so RETAIL_REC rises above the -24.2 trailing 28-day mean over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS prints below -25 in a weekly observation
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -5.3 at t-3w to -27.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -25 for four consecutive weekly prints while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below -24.2.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES climbed from -26.4 to -17.7 across t-3w to t-1w, showing office re-occupancy was already underway before the t-0 relapse to -29.9. A one-week interruption does not reverse an established commuting trend, so resumed weekday office presence restores lunchtime and after-work retail footfall and lifts RETAIL_REC above the -24.2 trailing mean within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 8.7 points from t-3w to t-1w before the t-0w dip
failure_condition: WORKPLACES stays at or below -29.9 for the next two weekly prints and the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below -24.2.
